In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in cases of PP and HRVA occurring on the same side, a translaminar screw would be a safer option than pedicle screws.
the pedicle width, pedicle length, and laminars are not adequate for a screw in the presence of PP+HRAVA.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in cases of PP, the pedicle width and laminar thickness are safe, whereas the pars length is not.
, in cases of ipsilateral PP+HRVA (3% prevalence in our study), a translaminar screw would be a safe option for C2 fixation.
in cases of PP and HRVA, C2 pedicles and pars length should be measured to assess construct safety before planning an atlas fixation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C2 pars and pedicle width should be carefully evaluated in patients with PP+HRVAs to avoid complications during surgery.
the presence of PP+HRVAs on the same side should be taken into account while planning C1-C2 fixation.
, in cases of PP and HRVA on the same side, C2 pars and pedicle screws are not a safe option.
